# BSD socket transport (spec v1.1) — implementation report
## Outcome
End-to-end implementation of `001.1-netimpl-bsd-socket.xml`. All nine sub-objectives in the spec landed. Public API broke as planned (no more `EventLoopGroup` / `SocketAddress` exposure). All three trait configurations build and test cleanly:
- default (NIO only): 65 tests pass. - NIO + BSDSocket: 68 tests pass (adds `BSDSocketTransportTests`). - BSDSocket only (`--disable-default-traits --traits BSDSocket`): 68 tests pass — existing `Listener integration` and `Mount simulation` suites run against `.bsdSocket` because that is `NFSTransport.default` in this trait configuration.
Manual end-to-end smoke against `NanoNFSDemo --transport=bsdSocket` accepts a raw RPC NULL CALL on `127.0.0.1:14049` and returns a well-formed `msg_type=REPLY, reply_status=ACCEPTED, accept_stat=SUCCESS` reply.
## Order followed (per spec §"작업 순서")
1. Sub-objective approval — confirmed via `AskUserQuestion`: full BSD impl (kqueue + per-connection driver), local-only build matrix verification, demo gains a `--transport=bsdSocket` flag. 2. README.md and CLAUDE.md updates first (CLAUDE.md §6 / §0 README-first rule). 3. Then `Package.swift`, `Sources/NanoNFS/Public/`, `Sources/NanoNFS/Transport/`, demo, tests.
## Sub-objective coverage
### §1 Public API: transport-agnostic listener
- New `Sources/NanoNFS/Public/NFSBoundAddress.swift` — `Sendable, Hashable` `(host, port)` struct. - `NFSServerListener.init` drops `eventLoopGroup`, gains `transport: NFSTransport = .default`. - `NFSServerListener.boundAddress` typed as `NFSBoundAddress?`. - README §4.6 rewritten end-to-end.
### §2 `NFSTransport` enum
- `Sources/NanoNFS/Public/NFSTransport.swift`. Cases: `.nio(eventLoopGroup:)` (NIO trait), `.bsdSocket` (BSDSocket trait), `.custom(any NFSTransportImplementation)`. Equatable intentionally not synthesised. - `NFSTransport.default` resolves to `.nio()` when both traits are on, `.bsdSocket` when only that trait is on. The case where neither trait is on is rejected at the package level by a top- level `#error` directive. - `NFSNIOEventLoopGroupBox` (NIO-only) for opt-in `EventLoopGroup` injection — same trade-off as documented in spec §2.
### §3 `NFSTransportImplementation` protocol + byte adapters
- Protocol in `NFSTransport.swift`. The closure parameters (`onBind`, `connectionHandler`) are inlined as `@escaping @Sendable` rather than carried by typealias — typealiased function parameters in Swift default to non-escaping and would prevent transports from capturing the closures into child Tasks. - `NFSAsyncByteStream` / `NFSAsyncByteWriter` in `NFSAsyncBytes.swift`. Both closure-backed: `NFSAsyncByteStream(next:)` takes an async-throws-returning closure; `NFSAsyncByteWriter(write:finish:)` takes the two obvious closures. Element type stays `NIOCore.ByteBuffer` because `NIOCore` is the unconditional baseline.
### §4 `NIOTransport` extracted
- `Sources/NanoNFS/Transport/NIOTransport.swift` (`#if NIO`). Holds the prior `ServerBootstrap` / `executeThenClose` body verbatim and adapts each accepted `NIOAsyncChannel` into a `NFSAsyncByteStream` / `NFSAsyncByteWriter` pair. EventLoopGroup ownership / shutdown logic preserved. - The NIO inbound iterator is wrapped in an `@unchecked Sendable` class (not an `actor`) because Swift 6 rejects mutating-async calls on actor-isolated stored properties.
### §5 `BSDSocketTransport` from scratch
- `Sources/NanoNFS/Transport/BSDSocketTransport.swift` (`#if BSDSOCKET`). Pure Swift Concurrency on top of `socket(2)` + `kqueue(2)` + `EVFILT_USER`. No GCD, no Network.framework.
- **One key deviation from the spec sketch:** the spec pseudocode ran the listener and per-connection `kevent(2)` blocking calls *inside* a Swift Concurrency `Task`. That deadlocked the test suite under parallel execution — eight tests × two blocking sites per test saturated the eight-thread cooperative pool, so per-connection Tasks could never run to feed the inbound stream. A `sample(1)` confirmed every cooperative thread parked in `kevent` / `recvfrom`.
- Resolution: blocking syscalls move off the cooperative pool. - The listener's accept loop runs on a dedicated `Thread` (real pthread). It yields accepted fds to an `AsyncStream`. Cancel arrives via `EVFILT_USER` from `withTaskCancellationHandler.onCancel`. - Each connection has its *own* dedicated `Thread` for the inbound read loop. Each `EVFILT_READ` wakeup drains `read(2)` to `EAGAIN` and yields chunks to an `AsyncThrowingStream`, which the cooperative consumer `Task` reads from. - Outbound `write(2)` happens inline on the calling Task. The common case (small RPC reply, kernel buffer not full) finishes in one shot. On `EAGAIN` the writer briefly hops onto a *one-shot* `Thread` to wait for `EVFILT_WRITE`, keeping the cooperative pool unblocked.
- **Two kqueues per connection** (`readKq`, `writeKq`). Each carries the same `EVFILT_USER` cancel ident, so a single `ConnectionContext.cancel()` wakes both halves at once. Avoids the subtle event-delivery edge cases of two threads calling `kevent(2)` concurrently on the same kq.
- **`@_silgen_name("kevent")` thunk** — `Darwin.kevent(...)` is ambiguous between the C struct `kevent` (initialiser) and the C function. Without `import NIOPosix` to disambiguate, the type-checker picks the struct initialiser and rejects the call. Same trick swift-nio uses internally.
- This deviates only in the *Swift execution context* that runs the kevent call, not in the syscall contract or cancellation model. The spec's "kqueue 직행이 자연스럽다" intent is honoured.
### §6 `Package.swift`
- `swift-tools-version: 6.2`. - Two traits: `NIO` (default-enabled), `BSDSocket`. Default array declared with `.default(enabledTraits: ["NIO"])`. - Baseline products (`NIOCore`, `NIOFoundationCompat`, `Logging`, `Atomics`) pulled unconditionally. `NIO` and `NIOPosix` gated on the `NIO` trait via `condition: .when(traits: ["NIO"])`. - `swiftSettings.define("NIO", .when(traits: ["NIO"]))` and `define("BSDSOCKET", .when(traits: ["BSDSocket"]))` — same across library, demo, test targets.
### §7 README + CLAUDE.md + task_logs
- `README.md` §2 rewritten: toolchain bump, traits table, dependency rules. §3 SYNOPSIS adds a `transport:` argument example. §4.6 rewritten end-to-end with the new types and a section on `NFSTransportImplementation`. - `CLAUDE.md` §2 directory layout adds `Transport/` with the revised dependency-direction diagram. §3 gains a new "Trait gating" subsection that codifies the file-level `#if` rule and the baseline-vs-gated dependency policy. - `task_logs/2026-05-09-bsdsocket-impl.md` written and linked from the §7 index.
### §8 Tests
- `BSDSocketTransportTests.swift` (trait-gated `#if BSDSOCKET`): three scenarios — RPC NULL round-trip, 32 pipelined NULL RPCs on a single connection, listener cancellation. - Existing `Listener integration` and `Mount simulation` suites adapted (just the `boundAddress` type change, `bound.port` no longer optional). They run against `.nio()` under `--traits NIO,BSDSocket` and `.bsdSocket` under `--disable-default-traits --traits BSDSocket`.
### §9 Out of scope
Honoured. No changes to `NFSServer` callbacks, no `ByteBuffer` decoupling from XDR / RPC / Wire, no NFSv3 work, no external- interface bind expansion.
## Verified locally
- `swift build` — clean for default, `--traits BSDSocket --disable-default-traits`, `--traits NIO,BSDSocket`. - `swift test` (and the same with each trait combination) — all tests pass. - End-to-end NULL RPC against `.build/.../NanoNFSDemo --transport=bsdSocket`.
## Items deferred
- **`mount_nfs` against the BSDSocket build.** CLAUDE.md §5 requires at least one real mount test per major surface. The NIO transport has the documented flow in README §5.5; the same flow should be exercised against `swift run --traits BSDSocket --disable-default-traits NanoNFSDemo --transport=bsdSocket`. Not done in this session. - **`ConnectionContext.cancel()` join races.** `close()` busy-waits on the read thread finishing (`while !t.isFinished { Thread.sleep(0.001) }`). Tests pass, but a proper completion semaphore or `pthread_join` would be cleaner.

# Cross-references
- Spec: `llm_prompts/features/001.1-netimpl-bsd-socket.xml`. - Confirmation entry: `task_logs/2026-05-09-bsdsocket-spec-v11.md`. - This-session implementation log: `task_logs/2026-05-09-bsdsocket-impl.md`. - v1.0 validation findings (kept for trace): `llm_prompts/features/001-netimpl-bsd-socket.execution-log.20260509.xml`.
# Behaviour notes worth capturing for future sessions
- The cooperative-thread-pool deadlock was only visible under parallel test execution. Single-test runs of `BSDSocketTransportTests` passed even with the original "blocking kevent inside a Task" implementation. Future regressions should run the full `swift test` suite (not `--filter`) under `--traits BSDSocket --disable-default-traits` to catch this. - swift-nio's `NIOPosix` happens to be available transitively even when the `NIO` trait is off (swiftpm resolves the package even without a trait-conditional dependency on a specific product). Tests that `import NIOPosix` therefore continue to compile under `--traits BSDSocket --disable-default-traits`. Not a problem today but worth knowing.
